snapshot: WHO African Region. Expanding national health insurance through Free Primary Healthcare and the 'Mahama Cares' reforms, and an outspoken voice for country-led global health after walking away from a US health compact.

agenda.title: Free Primary Healthcare and Mahama Cares
agenda.text: President Mahama launched the Free Primary Healthcare policy on 15 April 2026; the minister puts its cost at GH₵1.2 billion a year or more. The government is also linking the NHIS with the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (Mahama Cares), and earmarked GH₵32 billion for health in the 2026 budget.

agenda.title: Country-led global health, no US compact
agenda.text: Ghana's cabinet rejected the proposed five-year US health compact (up to US$109 million) in April 2026 over terms requiring the sharing of sensitive health data. At the World Health Summit in Berlin (October 2026) Minister Akandoh called for global health policies made with countries rather than for them, in the spirit of President Mahama's Accra Reset.

agenda.title: Health workforce and training
agenda.text: The ministry plans to decentralise specialist medical training across the country and is reviewing the governing party's health manifesto commitments with its agencies, including recruitment of nurses trained in 2022.

timeline.text: President Mahama launches the Free Primary Healthcare policy.
Cabinet rejects the proposed US health compact over data-sharing terms.
Minister Akandoh makes the case for global health equity at the World Health Assembly.
Government announces it will decentralise specialist medical training.
At the World Health Summit, Akandoh calls for country-led health systems; President Mahama is honoured for global health leadership.
Several digital health systems, including the national reporting platform DHIMS2, go offline; the opposition blames the minister.
